research_question: What is the effect of vasopressin type 2 receptor (V2R) antagonists compared with control (placebo or standard therapy) on serious adverse events in people with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease?
outcome_description: Incidence of serious adverse events (SAEs) in randomized participants
positive_direction: A positive effect indicates a lower risk of serious adverse events in the V2R antagonist group compared to control (favoring the intervention).
search_queries: vasopressin receptor antagonist autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease trial
tolvaptan ADPKD serious adverse events randomized controlled trial
V2 receptor antagonist polycystic kidney safety placebo trial
inclusion_criteria: Studies evaluating vasopressin type 2 receptor (V2R) antagonists (e.g., tolvaptan, lixivaptan, satavaptan) in individuals diagnosed with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD).
Studies including a concurrent control group receiving placebo or standard medical therapy.
Studies reporting quantitative data on serious adverse events (SAEs) or adverse event counts per randomized arm.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, editorials, commentaries, conference abstracts without data, and study protocols).
No comparison between a V2R antagonist intervention group and a concurrent control condition (e.g., single-arm trials).
No quantitative safety outcome data reporting serious adverse events (or counts per group allowing calculation of risk ratios).
Completely unrelated to vasopressin type 2 receptor antagonists or autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD).
moderators_to_extract: Specific V2R antagonist drug and dosing regimen
Baseline renal function / CKD stage or mean eGFR
Trial design and phase (Phase 2 vs Phase 3 RCT)
effect_size_note: Risk Ratio (RR) calculated from the number of patients experiencing at least one serious adverse event and total randomized sample size in each treatment arm.
